siblingDefinitions.prompt: Build Dark Volume as original standalone HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no runtime dependencies. The v4 thumbnail uses a 324×168 px native plane at reference origin (24,20) inside a 372×264 px light stage. Use the supplied 10×160 px recessed rail at (181,30), 48 px dark puck centered at (186,104), and 4×24 px orange indicator. Preserve SVGs 89-356.svg, 89-357.svg and 89-358.svg, including their shadows and root dimensions. The puck follows a vertical 54–166 px center range; the reference pose is about 55.36%. Full view uses a 400×584 px composition and the complete original 368×320 px virtual source plane. Retain the complete original 148 px plate, all 23 calibration dots and both endpoint ticks, the 104 px dark control and inner disc. Start at 0 on the original 0–100 integer range; rotation is −135 + 2.7 × value degrees. Preserve the original relative drag law: startValue + (dx − dy) × range / 150, followed by original step rounding and clamping. Arrow keys adjust one step; Home and End set the limits; Space advances and wraps. Keep the displayed heading and original description exactly, plus the guide “Drag or use arrow keys. Home / End set limits; Space advances.” Adapt the entire plate and calibration geometry on short stages, maintaining 44 px minimum targets, at least 11 px rendered type, and gaps between copy, control, readout, guide and shared Dock. Keep source inputs outside retained paint. Drag follows directly with bounded rubber banding; release and key changes use stiffness 380, damping 32 and mass 1. Reduced motion uses 150 ms retained-paint fades. Support independent caller, document and viewport holds, ordered queued intent, captured cancellation, visible focus against the actual backing material, and complete inert cleanup. The Stage owns the Drag action and replay controls. Keep exact sparse Figma sizing; document its fill exception rather than enlarging the artwork. Use only the supplied local SVGs and fonts, neutral materials and the single orange accent.

siblingDefinitions.prompt: Build Line Volume as original standalone HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no runtime dependencies. The v4 thumbnail uses a 324×168 px native plane at reference origin (24,20) inside a 372×264 px light stage. Use the supplied 1×161 px hairline stroke, 40×6 px slim handle centered at (186,107), and exact −12 dB caption. Preserve SVGs 89-377.svg, 89-378.svg and 89-380.svg, including their root dimensions. Keep the captured zero-opacity fill absent. Scale only the caption wrapper enough to render at least 11 px; after interaction, show the selected value in local Geist Mono. The native range is −24–0 dB, with handle centers from 184 to 30 px. Full view uses a 400×584 px composition and the complete original 368×320 px virtual source plane. Retain the complete original 114 px round plate, 88 px white rotary control and orange line. Start at 50 on the original 0–100 integer range; rotation is −135 + 2.7 × value degrees. Preserve the original relative drag law: startValue + (dx − dy) × range / 150, followed by original step rounding and clamping. Arrow keys adjust one step; Home and End set the limits; Space advances and wraps. Keep the displayed heading and original description exactly, plus the guide “Drag or use arrow keys. Home / End set limits; Space advances.” Adapt the entire plate and calibration geometry on short stages, maintaining 44 px minimum targets, at least 11 px rendered type, and gaps between copy, control, readout, guide and shared Dock. Keep source inputs outside retained paint. Drag follows directly with bounded rubber banding; release and key changes use stiffness 380, damping 32 and mass 1. Reduced motion uses 150 ms retained-paint fades. Support independent caller, document and viewport holds, ordered queued intent, captured cancellation, visible focus against the actual backing material, and complete inert cleanup. The Stage owns the Drag action and replay controls. Keep exact sparse Figma sizing; document its fill exception rather than enlarging the artwork. Use only the supplied local SVGs and fonts, neutral materials and the single orange accent.
